To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the CCTV operators at Schiphol do not have a clear idea about what is normal and what is deviant, and that they use a lot of time to look at the monitors, but that they are not very interested in the images.

the Military Police at Amsterdam Airport Schiplhol use routine and retrospective surveillance, that they rely on the expertise of their CCTV operators, that they use the camera as a tool for communication with the public, that they are not very interested in the ‘heterotopic’ qualities of CCTV, and that they use CCTV as a tool for their own professional development.
the CCTV operators at Schiphol do not have a clear definition of what constitutes normal behavior at the airport.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the operators in the Military Police’s control room at Schiphol deal with the absence of a fixed point of orientation in the airport.
the practices of CCTV operators at an international airport, and shows that the use of CCTV does not always fit the categories identified by the literature on CCTV.
the ‘heterotopias’ of CCTV surveillance, which we define as places where the CCTV operators are confronted with a lack of normality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CCTV-operator practices at the Military Police control room at Schiphol are a form of heterotopia.
CCTV is not used as a tool to spot the deviant but to spot the normal, and that it is not used for prevention or detection but for control and management.
Schiphol is a ‘heterotopia’.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CCTV operators are constantly zooming in on ‘heterotopias’, places that are ‘out of place’.
the operators at Schiphol have to deal with a ‘heterotopic’ space.
the operators are ‘zooming in on heterotopia’ (Foucault, in Rabinow 1984).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the operators’ work practices are not only about the use of technical means, but also about the social and cultural context in which the technical surveillance system operates.
, in order to understand CCTV surveillance practices at airports, we need to focus on the practices behind the screen.
, in order to understand CCTV surveillance, it is necessary to look beyond the screen.
